clue.text: Award English poet received eleven years ago?

indicators.note: the poet's name receives, or takes in, the date written in Roman numerals

parts.note: Thomas Gray, the English poet of the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
the puzzle appeared in 2011, so eleven years earlier was 2000, MM in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A question about some English poet who won a prize over a decade back.
explanation.walkthrough: The date clue depends on when the puzzle ran: it appeared in 2011, so eleven years earlier was the year 2000. 'received' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A Grammy is the prize handed out each year by the American recording academy.

clue.text: Creature needing to take food tucked into fruit

indicators.note: the eating word is put inside the fruit, as if tucked into it

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
to eat is to take food

explanation.surface: An animal that must eat, its food stuffed into some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' also suggests eating heartily, but here it signals one piece placed inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A great ape is one of the large primates such as a gorilla or chimpanzee, animals.

clue.text: Went into foreign land — easy!

indicators.note: foreign means strange or alien, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone travelled abroad and found it no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges LAND and EASY.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into a matter is to examine it in detail, as an analyst does.

clue.text: Unbecoming of doctor to consume a drink right before work

indicators.note: the doctor's word consumes, or takes in, the rest

parts.note: of doctor is the doctor's, MO's, MO being a medical officer

indicators.note: before puts the right letter ahead of the work word

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: It is unseemly for a doctor to down a drink just before going to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of doctor' stands for the possessive doctor's, an MO's; 'to consume' signals the container, and 'before' orders the right and work pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Malapropos means inappropriate or out of place, unfitting.

clue.text: Was circulating advertisements (flyers)

parts.note: saw is a past form, like was, read here as the past of see
bills are posters or leaflets handed round to advertise

explanation.surface: Someone recalls seeing adverts being handed about, the flyers of the parenthesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyers' looks like a gloss on the advertisements, but it is the definition: sawbills are diving ducks, birds that fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbills are ducks such as mergansers with serrated beaks, and birds are flyers.

clue.text: Cunning wife set scholar straight

indicators.note: cunning means crafty or devious, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crafty wife puts an academic right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunning' rearranges WIFE, SET and SCHOLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the shortest direct route between two places, in a beeline.

clue.text: Place to sleep for cobblers

explanation.definitionFit: A narrow shelf bed is one sense; British slang 'cobblers' means nonsense, the other sense.

clue.text: No ice in sweet alcoholic drink

indicators.note: no means without, so the word for ice is removed from the sweet

parts.note: liquorice is a black chewy sweet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweet alcoholic drink served without ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like it describes the drink, but it is a noun: the confection LIQUORICE, from which ICE goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor means spirits or any strong alcohol.

clue.text: Get warm, then hot after appearance of sun? Protection needed

indicators.note: after says the other pieces follow the opening letter
the first appearance of the word is its opening letter

parts.note: to heat is to get warm
H is short for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Advice to warm up and then sweat in the sun, with protection needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearance of sun' gives S, which goes first because HEAT and H come 'after' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a protective cover, as for a blade.

clue.text: Seeing old structure in Berlin collapsing

parts.note: seeing, as in seeing a doctor, is going to
the Berlin Wall divided the city until 1989

explanation.surface: Visiting the remains of the Berlin Wall as it falls down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' seems part of the scene, but it is the definition of an idiom for a business failing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being ruined or failing, as a bankrupt business does.

clue.text: First signs of Eire's major trouble revealed by brief communication

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words that follow are taken

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A short message reveals the start of a big crisis in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic message sent by computer is usually a short note.

clue.text: Fruit that's yellow and brown: one which comes from France

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow
tan is a light brown colour
I is the Roman numeral for one
que is French for which

explanation.surface: A description of a fruit's colours, with one imported from France.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic term for gold, and QUE is the French for 'which', hence 'from France'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ortanique is a Jamaican citrus hybrid of orange and tangerine.

clue.text: Small dog: one plays with it if relaxing

indicators.note: relaxing means loosening the order of the letters so they can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A small pet dog is the sort somebody plays with when unwinding.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'one plays with it' as a description of the dog's purpose; 'relaxing' loosens the letters of ONE, PLAYS and IT into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy spaniel is one of the miniature breeds kept as lapdogs, like the King Charles.

clue.text: Potential to make a leap?

explanation.definitionFit: Electrical potential is measured in this unit; in riding and fencing the same word is a sideways leap or turn.

clue.text: Reckoned daughter's put out, finding you ensconced in bed and breakfast

indicators.note: the old word for you is settled inside the shortened word
put out means the daughter's letter is removed

parts.note: guessed means reckoned
D is short for daughter
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: Someone guessed a daughter was upset to find you snug in a B&B.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' takes D from GUESSED, leaving GUESSE, and THOU goes 'ensconced in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hotel offering lodging and morning meals is a guesthouse.

clue.text: Outrageous publicity theatre company adopted to attract unlimited audience

indicators.note: the theatre company is taken into, or adopted by, the publicity word

parts.note: a poster is a piece of publicity on a wall
rep is short for repertory, a theatre company

indicators.note: unlimited means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a house is the audience in a theatre

explanation.surface: Garish publicity is taken up by a theatre company hoping to draw a full house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted' signals the theatre company taken inside the publicity word; 'unlimited' strips the audience word of its outer letters; 'to attract' just joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurdly unreasonable or shocking is outrageous.

clue.text: Giving account in foreign language? German gets upset about that

indicators.note: the reversed German abbreviation goes about the language
upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: Latin is a language foreign to English speakers

explanation.surface: Telling a story in some other tongue, which upsets a German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GER into REG, which goes 'about' LATIN; 'that' points back to the foreign language.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating a story means narrating or recounting it.

clue.text: Briefly mock boy's inability to think rationally

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: mock means sham, unreal
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A short taunt at a lad who cannot think straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' cuts UNREAL to UNREA; the 's of boy's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreason is the lack of reason or sound judgement.

clue.text: Wasted hours with tweets — unknown number from Cornwall area?

indicators.note: wasted means spoiled or ruined, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: n is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Someone frittering hours on social media posts to a stranger in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' rearranges HOURS and TWEETS to SOUTHWESTER, and N is added. Cornwall is the county at the far south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornwall lies in the far south-west of England, so a thing from there is of that region.

clue.text: Turning up late, practitioner accepts reprimand

indicators.note: Turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
accepts means the words hold the answer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A late professional takes a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'accepts reprimand' as the definition, but 'accepts' is the hidden-word signal: 'late, practitioner' holds TEPRAC, which 'Turning up' reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for calling them in for a telling-off.

clue.text: French footballer's hairstyle shown in supporters' mag

indicators.note: the hairstyle is shown inside the magazine word

parts.note: a zine, from fanzine, is a supporters' magazine
a DA, or duck's arse, is a slicked-back hairstyle

explanation.surface: A footballer's haircut is featured in a fan magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of footballer's is 'has'. A DA is a 1950s quiffed hairstyle, slang for duck's arse.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinedine Zidane is the celebrated French midfielder who won the 1998 World Cup.

clue.text: A number backing alliance of nations

indicators.note: backing means the word for the number is read backwards

parts.note: six is a number

explanation.surface: A count of countries supporting an international bloc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' means the number is read backwards after the A; the definition is the wartime bloc.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the Second World War alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan.

clue.text: Harrow's principal teacher worried about a learner's treatment

indicators.note: principal means first, so the leading letter of the school name is taken
the rearranged teacher letters go about, or around, the other two
worried means agitated, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Harrow's headmaster frets over a pupil's medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges TEACHER into ETHCARE, which goes 'about' A and L after the E. Harrow is a famous English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Healthcare is the medical treatment and services that keep people well.

clue.text: Bishop shirks extra responsibility

indicators.note: shirks means the bishop avoids, so its letter is left out

parts.note: a bonus is an extra
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop dodges additional duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shirks' removes B from BONUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty.

clue.text: Not a dish pal cooked during winter month, except for starters

indicators.note: cooked means altered or fiddled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: in means during, as in the night
Jan is short for January, a winter month in the north

indicators.note: for starters means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A friend cooks something that is no dish in January, apart from the starters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' is slang for an attractive person, so the definition is someone unglamorous. 'cooked' rearranges PAL into PLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain-looking woman is slangily the opposite of a dish, an attractive person.

clue.text: Military groups of upper-class twits?

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class usage
nits are fools or twits

explanation.surface: A jibe that army regiments are full of posh idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: U is a long-standing British label for upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Army formations such as battalions and companies are military units.

clue.text: Those people will stop girl going round part of Greece

indicators.note: the reversed girl stops a gap, filling the middle of the other word

parts.note: they means those people

indicators.note: going round means the word for girl is turned back to front

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Some people block a girl travelling around a region of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns the girl backwards, and 'will stop' puts the result in the middle of the people word, as a stopper fills a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Thessaly is a region of central Greece.

clue.text: Acting president?

parts.note: acting usually means standing in for someone; here it means a former film actor who became US head of state

explanation.definitionFit: The fortieth US president had been a Hollywood film actor before politics.
